# Aptabase — Tauri Plugin

> Tauri plugin for Aptabase: open-source, privacy-first analytics for desktop and mobile apps built with Tauri v2.

Rust Crate: `tauri-plugin-aptabase`
Install (Rust): `cargo add tauri-plugin-aptabase`
npm Package: `@aptabase/tauri`
Install (JS): `npm add @aptabase/tauri`
Repo: https://github.com/aptabase/tauri-plugin-aptabase

## Overview

Aptabase is an open-source, privacy-first analytics platform. This plugin integrates Aptabase into Tauri v2 apps.

- Get your App Key from the Aptabase dashboard (Settings > Instructions)
- App keys follow the format `A-EU-*` (European) or `A-US-*` (US)
- Only strings and numbers are allowed as custom property values
- All tracking is non-blocking and runs in the background
- No events are tracked automatically — you must call `track_event`/`trackEvent` manually
- The plugin automatically captures OS, app version, locale, and other system properties

## Important: Dual API (Rust + JavaScript)

This plugin provides **two APIs** — use whichever fits your app architecture:

- **Rust API** — use `EventTracker` trait on `App`, `AppHandle`, or `Window`
- **JavaScript API** — use `trackEvent()` from `@aptabase/tauri` in your webview frontend

Both APIs require the Rust plugin to be registered in your Tauri builder. The JS API calls the Rust backend via Tauri's IPC.

## Installation

### 1. Add the Rust crate

In `src-tauri/Cargo.toml`:

```toml
[dependencies]
tauri-plugin-aptabase = "1.3.0"
```

### 2. Add the JS package (optional, for webview tracking)

```bash
npm add @aptabase/tauri
```

### 3. Register the plugin

In `src-tauri/src/main.rs` (or `lib.rs`):

```rust
#[tokio::main]
async fn main() {
    tauri::Builder::default()
        .plugin(tauri_plugin_aptabase::Builder::new("<YOUR_APP_KEY>").build())
        .run(tauri::generate_context!())
        .expect("error while running tauri application");
}
```

### 4. Add ACL permission

Add `aptabase:allow-track-event` to your Tauri capabilities to allow the JS API to send events, and `aptabase:allow-track-error` to report errors. In your `src-tauri/capabilities/*.json`:

```json
{
  "permissions": ["aptabase:allow-track-event", "aptabase:allow-track-error"]
}
```

## Track Events (Rust)

Import the `EventTracker` trait and call `track_event` on `App`, `AppHandle`, or `Window`:

```rust
use tauri_plugin_aptabase::EventTracker;

// Event with no properties
app.track_event("app_started", None);

// Event with properties (serde_json::Value)
app.track_event("screen_view", Some(serde_json::json!({ "name": "Settings" })));
```

Full example with startup and exit events:

```rust
use tauri_plugin_aptabase::EventTracker;

#[tokio::main]
async fn main() {
    tauri::Builder::default()
        .plugin(tauri_plugin_aptabase::Builder::new("<YOUR_APP_KEY>").build())
        .setup(|app| {
            app.track_event("app_started", None);
            Ok(())
        })
        .build(tauri::generate_context!())
        .expect("error while running tauri application")
        .run(|handler, event| match event {
            tauri::RunEvent::Exit { .. } => {
                handler.track_event("app_exited", None);
                handler.flush_events_blocking();
            }
            _ => {}
        });
}
```

## Track Events (JavaScript)

```js
import { trackEvent } from "@aptabase/tauri";

trackEvent("app_started");
```

## Track Events with Properties (JavaScript)

```js
import { trackEvent } from "@aptabase/tauri";

trackEvent("screen_view", { name: "Settings" });
trackEvent("purchase", { plan: "pro", price: 9.99 });
```

## Error Reporting (beta)

Reports appear on the `Errors` page of the Aptabase dashboard. Errors count against a separate monthly error quota.

Report a handled error from Rust with the `ErrorTracker` trait (implemented for `App`, `AppHandle`, and `Window`):

```rust
use tauri_plugin_aptabase::{ErrorReport, ErrorTracker};

app.track_error(&err); // any std::error::Error: its type name, message and causes
app.track_error_report(ErrorReport::from_error(&err).with_fatal(true)); // severity: fatal
app.track_error_report(ErrorReport::new("SyncConflict", "two devices edited the same note"));
```

Report a handled error from JavaScript (needs the `aptabase:allow-track-error` permission):

```js
import { trackError } from "@aptabase/tauri";

try {
  await saveSettings();
} catch (error) {
  trackError(error); // severity: error
  // trackError(error, { fatal: true }) for errors the app can't recover from
}
```

Report crashes and uncaught errors automatically:

```rust
tauri::Builder::default()
    .plugin(tauri_plugin_aptabase::Builder::new("<YOUR_APP_KEY>").with_crash_reporting().build())
```

- A panic on the main thread is a fatal `crash`; the app waits up to 3 seconds for the report before it exits
- A panic in an async command or a task on Tauri's async runtime is a `taskException`; one on another thread is `unhandled` (both severity `error`)
- The webview's uncaught errors (`unhandled`) and unhandled promise rejections (`taskException`) are reported too, with the `aptabase:allow-track-error` permission
- Reports are sent immediately, one per request; network errors, 408, 429 and 5xx are retried, a 403 (quota exhausted) is dropped

## Configuration

The `Builder` accepts optional `InitOptions`:

```rust
use tauri_plugin_aptabase::{Builder, InitOptions};
use std::time::Duration;

tauri::Builder::default()
    .plugin(
        Builder::new("<YOUR_APP_KEY>")
            .with_options(InitOptions {
                host: Some("https://your-self-hosted-instance.com".into()), // self-hosted only (A-SH-* keys)
                flush_interval: Some(Duration::from_secs(30)), // custom flush interval
            })
            .build()
    )
```

- `host` — required only for self-hosted Aptabase instances (app keys starting with `A-SH-*`)
- `flush_interval` — defaults to 60s in release, 2s in debug mode
- Events are batched and flushed periodically; `flush_events_blocking()` forces an immediate flush
- Up to 25 events per request; network failures and 5xx responses keep the events queued for the next flush, other unsuccessful responses drop them
- Requests use the system proxy settings (macOS, Windows) and the `HTTP_PROXY` / `HTTPS_PROXY` / `ALL_PROXY` / `NO_PROXY` environment variables

## TLS Backend

Cargo features choose the TLS backend: `default-tls` (default, rustls), `rustls-tls`, or `native-tls` (OpenSSL on Linux and Android). To switch, turn off the default features:

```toml
tauri-plugin-aptabase = { version = "1.3", default-features = false, features = ["native-tls"] }
```

## Platform Notes

- Requires Tauri v2 (2.x)
- Rust edition 2021, MSRV 1.85
- The `EventTracker` trait is implemented for `App`, `AppHandle`, and `Window`
- The JS `trackEvent` is async but you don't need to await it
- `Builder::with_crash_reporting()` reports panics and the webview's uncaught errors; a custom panic hook can still be set via `Builder::with_panic_hook()`

## Cross-Discovery

For all Aptabase SDKs and documentation, see: https://aptabase.com/llms.txt
